parsed_record.title: Klavžar–Tian–Tuite complexity conjecture for Builder/Blocker games
parsed_record.statement:
Consider the Builder/Blocker games denoted by the B-game and B'-game, together with their decision versions. **Klavžar–Tian–Tuite's conjecture.** The decision versions of the B- and B'-games are PSPACE-complete.

The complexity of these decision problems was described as completely unknown before this conjecture. The conjectured PSPACE-completeness remains open.
parsed_record.source_name: Ullas Chandran S. V., Sandi Klavžar and James Tuite, “The General Position Problem: A Survey”, arXiv:2501.19385 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19385

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2025). “Another open problem is given in the following conjectured Nordhaus-Gaddum relation.”

parsed_record.title: Uniqueness of minimal presentations of q-transversal matroids
parsed_record.statement: Let $M$ be a $q$-transversal matroid with a presentation by a system of subspaces. A presentation is **minimal** if no member can be replaced by a proper subspace while preserving the represented matroid. **Uniqueness of minimal presentations.** Minimal presentations are unique. The claim is stated without evidence of resolution in the supplied text and is therefore open.
parsed_record.source_name: Mark Saaltink, “A theory of q-transversals”, arXiv:2503.12201 (2025).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12201

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

parsed_record.title: The conf-configuration invariance conjecture for $h(w)$
parsed_record.statement:
Let $A$ be a vertex and let $v,w$ be $A$-generic words, meaning that their arc-configuration sets equal the set defining $A$. **The conf-configuration invariance conjecture.**

$$
h(v)=h(w).
$$

Equivalently, if $\mathrm{Conf}(v)=\mathrm{Conf}(w)$, then $h(v)=h(w)$. The paper proves this for admissible $A$-generic words and conjectures that admissibility can be omitted.
parsed_record.source_name: Andrei Grigorev and Evgeny Mukhin, “On representations of quantum affine sl_2”, arXiv:2505.11605 (2025).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11605

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

parsed_record.title: Binary matroid conjecture for matroids with cycle systems
parsed_record.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid admitting a **cycle system**, meaning a cycle-system structure as defined in the source. **Binary matroid conjecture.** Every matroid with a cycle system is binary. The source notes that all known examples admitting cycle systems are regular and relates cycle systems to the underlying circuit space. Whether nonbinary examples exist remains open.
parsed_record.source_name: Scott Corry, Anton Dochtermann, Solís McClain, David Perkinson and Lixing Yi, “Cycle systems, coparking functions, and h-vectors of matroids”, arXiv:2509.11460 (2025).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.11460

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).

parsed_record.title: Hassler–Treglown conjecture on maximal independent sets in graphs with a perfect matching
parsed_record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma)$ denote its number of maximal independent sets. **Hassler–Treglown conjecture.** If $\Gamma$ contains a perfect matching, then

$$
\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma)\leq 2^{n/2}.
$$

The abstract states that this conjecture is resolved by the paper’s graph-theoretic bound.
parsed_record.source_name: József Balogh, Ramon I. Garcia, Hong Liu and Ningyuan Yang, “Infinitely many groups exhibiting intermediate growth in maximal sum-free sets”, arXiv:2509.19248 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19248

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2025).

parsed_record.title: Bajo et al.'s leading-coefficient conjecture for trees
parsed_record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\widetilde{\chi}_G^\mathbbm{1}(q,x)$ denote the polynomial introduced in the source for the linear form $\mathbbm{1}=(1,1,\ldots,1)$. **Bajo et al.'s conjecture.** The leading coefficient of $\widetilde{\chi}_G^\mathbbm{1}(q,x)$ distinguishes trees. The source attributes this conjecture to Bajo et al.; its resolution is not specified here.
parsed_record.source_name: Matthias Beck, Benjamin Braun and Alvaro Cornejo, “Generating functions of q-chromatic polynomials”, arXiv:2509.22946 (2025).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.22946

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).

parsed_record.title: Conjectured value of the uniformly dense Turán density of the four-vertex star
parsed_record.statement:
Let $S_4$ be the four-vertex star $3$-graph, and let $\pi_{\mathrm{V}}(S_4)$ denote the corresponding Turán-density parameter. **Conjecture for the four-vertex star.**

$$
\pi_{\mathrm{V}}(S_4)=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

This is the second conjecture announced in the concluding remarks, following the paper's results for the other parameter ranges; no resolution is supplied in the given text.
parsed_record.source_name: Hao Lin and Wenling Zhou, “Turán density of stars in uniformly dense hypergraphs”, arXiv:2510.12576 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.12576

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2025). “However, determining $\piv(F)$ of a given $3$-graph $F$ is also very challenging. For instance, the conjecture that $\piv(K^{(3)}_4)=1/2$ has remained a open problem in this area since R\"odl proposed a quasi-random construction in 1986.”

parsed_record.title: The b-chromatic number of the tensor product of distinct star graphs
parsed_record.statement: Let $G$ be the tensor product of two distinct star graphs $S_n$ and $S_m$. **Star-graph tensor-product conjecture.** The $b$-chromatic number of $G$ is $m+n+1$. This conjecture proposes a general formula for the $b$-chromatic number of tensor products of distinct star graphs; the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
parsed_record.source_name: Erik Dahlen, “On the b-chromatic number of star graph operators”, arXiv:2510.18265 (2025).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18265

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).

parsed_record.title: Basis conjecture for the box-kernel relations
parsed_record.statement: For positive integers $z,d$ with $z\leq d$, let $\mathcal{K}_{z,d}$ and $\operatorname{Box}_{z,d}$ be as defined in the source. **Basis conjecture.** If $z\leq d$, then $\mathcal{K}_{z,d}$ is a basis of $\operatorname{ker}\operatorname{Box}_{z,d}$. This refines the box-kernel conjecture by asserting linear independence as well as spanning; the paper gives no proof in general.
parsed_record.source_name: Benjamin Brindle, “On the structure of Multiple q-Zeta Values”, arXiv:2511.07302 (2025).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.07302

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

parsed_record.title: Favaron's forbidden-subgraph conjecture for irredundance perfect graphs
parsed_record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $P_6$, $G_1$, and $G_2$ be the graphs described in Figure 5 of the source. **Favaron's conjecture.** If $G$ does not contain $P_6$, $G_1$, or $G_2$ as induced subgraphs, then $G$ is irredundance perfect. The conjecture was later completely proved, and a stronger result is known using $P_6$, $G_1$, and $G_5$ instead; it is therefore solved.
parsed_record.source_name: Vadim Zverovich, Pavel Skums and Lutz Volkmann, “A Characterization of P_6-Free Irredundance Perfect Graphs”, arXiv:2603.14668 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14668

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2026); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

parsed_record.title: Puech's forbidden-subgraph conjecture for irredundance perfect graphs
parsed_record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $P_6$, $G_4$, and $G_5$ be the graphs described in Figure 5 of the source. **Puech's conjecture.** If $G$ does not contain $P_6$, $G_4$, or $G_5$ as induced subgraphs, then $G$ is irredundance perfect. The supplied text introduces this as a generalization of the preceding conjectures but gives no resolution of it, so its status remains open.
parsed_record.source_name: Vadim Zverovich, Pavel Skums and Lutz Volkmann, “A Characterization of P_6-Free Irredundance Perfect Graphs”, arXiv:2603.14668 (2026).

parsed_record.title: Seven-color packing coloring conjecture for claw-free subcubic graphs
parsed_record.statement: Let $G$ be a claw-free subcubic graph. **Seven-color packing coloring conjecture.** The graph $G$ is $(2,2,2,2,2,2,2)$-packing colorable. The paper gives related packing-coloring results for claw-free subcubic graphs, but does not establish this seven-color assertion; it remains open.
parsed_record.source_name: Ayman El Zein and Maidoun Mortada, “Impact of local girth on the S-packing coloring of k-saturated subcubic graphs”, arXiv:2603.25113 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25113

parsed_record.title: Monotonicity conjecture for induced saturation in the hypergrid
parsed_record.statement: Let $P$ be a poset, and consider the induced saturation function $\mathrm{sat}^{\star}([t]^n,P)$ whenever it is defined. **Monotonicity conjecture.** The function $(n,t)\mapsto\mathrm{sat}^{\star}([t]^n,P)$ is monotone non-decreasing in both $n$ and $t$ over its domain. The supplied text gives no resolution of this natural monotonicity claim.
parsed_record.source_name: R. Altar Ciceksiz, Victor Falgas-Ravry, Sabrina Lato and Maryam Sharifzadeh, “Induced poset saturation in the hypergrid”, arXiv:2604.12641 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12641

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2026). “This was recently proved independently by Bastide, Hodor, La and Trotter and by Ivan, Fl\'idr and Jaffe .”

parsed_record.title: Stacking–estimating equality for finite connected trees
parsed_record.statement:
Let $T$ be a finite connected tree. **Stacking–estimating conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{stack}(T)=\operatorname{estim}(T).
$$

The statement is presented as an immediate consequence of the preceding theorem under ASH, which gives the corresponding upper bound. The equality remains unresolved in the supplied source context.
parsed_record.source_name: Tamás Csernák and Lajos Soukup, “Stacking and clearing in graph pebbling”, arXiv:2604.22341 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.22341

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2026).

parsed_record.title: Properness of the hierarchy of graph classes $\mathcal{G}_k$
parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}_k$ be the graph class defined in the paper for each $k\in\mathbb{N}$. **Hierarchy properness conjecture.** For each $k\in\mathbb{N}$, the inclusion

$$
\mathcal{G}_k\subseteq\mathcal{G}_{k+1}
$$

is proper. The conjecture asserts that the hierarchy of these graph classes never collapses; the supplied text gives no resolution status beyond the claim itself.
parsed_record.source_name: Duncan Adamson, Amanita Dietz, Pamela Fleischmann, Annika Huch and Silas Cato Sacher, “2-word-π-representable Graphs”, arXiv:2605.27183 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27183

parsed_record.title: The thick-hook meld conjecture
parsed_record.statement: A **thick hook** is the thick-hook family of partitions used in CRIM, and a **meld** is the partition operation defined in the paper. A losing position is a $\mathcal P$-position. **Thick-hook meld conjecture.** A meld of losing thick hooks is losing. This proposes that the losing-position property is preserved by melding thick hooks; the source gives no resolution.
parsed_record.source_name: Ina Bašić, Eric Gottlieb and Matjaž Krnc, “CRIM: A Natural Game on Integer Partitions”, arXiv:2606.16828 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16828

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

parsed_record.title: Quadraticity conjecture for matroid base polytopes
parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a matroid with basis polytope $P_B(\mathcal{M})$, and let $I_{P_B(\mathcal{M})}$ be its toric ideal.

**Matroid-base quadraticity conjecture.** The toric ideal $I_{P_B(\mathcal{M})}$ is quadratic.

This is presented as a weaker version of White's conjecture. The source does not give resolution evidence for this weaker statement, so its status is recorded as open.
parsed_record.source_name: Aki Mori and Hidefumi Ohsugi, “Simplex faces and quadratic toric ideals of lattice polytopes”, arXiv:2606.20430 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20430

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2026). “In , a long-standing conjecture ``the toric ideal of any matroid polytope has a quadratic Gr\"obner basis" is disproved.”

parsed_record.title: He–et al. complete multipartite chromatic-choosability conjecture
parsed_record.statement: A **complete $k$-partite graph** is a graph whose vertices are partitioned into $k$ independent parts, with every pair of vertices in distinct parts adjacent. **He et al.'s conjecture.** Any complete $k$-partite graph $G$ with $n(G)=2k+1$ is chromatic-choosable. This is presented as a complete-multipartite reformulation of Ohba's conjecture and is therefore resolved by the same result.
parsed_record.source_name: Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram and N Narayanan, “List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability – A Dynamic Survey”, arXiv:2606.31702 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31702

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

parsed_record.title: Havet et al.'s list square coloring conjecture for planar graphs
parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $G^2$ denote its **square**, in which two vertices are adjacent when their distance in $G$ is at most two. **Havet et al.'s conjecture.** For any planar graph $G$,

$$
\chi_\ell(G^2)=\chi(G^2).
$$

This is the planar-graph specialization of list square coloring; the supplied text says the conjecture was later disproved by Hasanvand.
parsed_record.source_name: Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram and N Narayanan, “List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability – A Dynamic Survey”, arXiv:2606.31702 (2026).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31702

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2026); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

parsed_record.title: Mullin's root-of-unity conjecture for uniform mixing
parsed_record.statement: Let $X$ be a graph, and suppose that $X$ admits uniform mixing at time $t$. **Mullin's conjecture.** Then $e^{it}$ is a root of unity. This conjecture concerns an arithmetic constraint on potential uniform-mixing times; the source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
parsed_record.source_name: Xiwang Cao and Cuiwen Zhu, “Uniform mixing and ε-uniform mixing on cycles”, arXiv:2607.04207 (2026).
